products.title: Read the claim. Find the study. Keep the limits.
products.description: A practical workbook for turning a repurposing headline into a precise question, a source trail and a useful discussion checklist.
scope: Question framing; source types; matching population and endpoint; reading numbers; claim worksheet; conversation preparation
chapters: Keep the source and the claim separate
Compare the question with the study
Read the result faithfully
Build a small evidence map
Complete your claim worksheet
Prepare a focused conversation
products.readiness: Complete original eight-page evidence-reading draft, edition 0.3, with a three-page preview and one-page summary generated from the same editable manuscript. Independent editorial, clinical and legal review, accessible PDF tagging and reader testing remain release requirements.

products.title: Long COVID research: prevention, treatment and symptom claims
products.description: A structured reading companion that keeps acute-infection prevention studies separate from trials in established illness and from symptom-specific claims.
scope: Separate prevention/treatment tracks; metformin; nirmatrelvir with ritonavir; fluvoxamine; fatigue versus cognition endpoints; formulation and access questions; null findings and harms
chapters: Prevention and established illness are separate questions
Match symptom, recovery and diagnosis outcomes
What each acquired report can and cannot answer
Corrections, missing full texts and unresolved appraisal
A source-linked comparison, without a treatment ranking
Questions and a printable discussion worksheet
products.readiness: Current selected sources and findings offer a starting point, but broader returns and formal appraisal remain incomplete.

products.title: Repurposed drugs and cancer claims: a reading companion
products.description: A family-facing guide to distinguish laboratory predictions, case reports and patient trials, and organize questions for an oncology discussion.
scope: Cancer-type and stage boundaries; primary versus secondary sources; concurrent treatment; clinical outcomes versus model endpoints; misleading headlines; discussion worksheet
chapters: Recognize the exact cancer context in a claim
Separate models, early studies and comparative human reports
Read the outcome, comparison and treatment setting
Find corrections and missing original evidence
Keep standard care and research participation distinct
Prepare questions for the oncology team
products.readiness: A workflow guide is feasible earlier than a drug-ranking handbook, but cancer examples need original-source verification and qualified oncology review.

products.title: Pramipexole and depression: reading the evidence
products.description: A guide to the questions readers ask about depression, anhedonia, response timing, adverse effects and access, with clear limits on indirect comparisons.
scope: Treatment-resistant depression and anhedonia; comparator/augmentation context; response timing; adverse effects and discontinuation questions; prescribing-access context
chapters: Define the depression population and prior treatments
Read comparison groups and outcome measures
Separate a response signal from a supported conclusion
Find the limits of the tolerability record
Check access questions without prescribing advice
Complete a source and discussion worksheet
products.readiness: Strong relative interest in this bounded demand sample; the existing site context does not provide an appraised depression evidence guide.

products.title: Low-dose naltrexone: research, formulations and access
products.description: A practical evidence guide separating the reason for use, the preparation supplied and the outcomes actually studied.
scope: Separate chronic-symptom indications; formulations and compounding questions; controlled studies and nonresponse; cost/access questions with dated jurisdictional scope
chapters: Match the condition and formulation studied
Separate original reports from anecdotal claims
Read the outcomes and limits for each specific use
Document gaps in safety and interaction coverage
Understand the scope of access questions
Prepare a source-linked discussion checklist
products.readiness: Demand signals exist, but the current accepted CP28 context has no matching evidentiary pair for this scope. New source identities are not a completed synthesis.

products.title: Itraconazole in cancer research: questions by cancer type
products.description: A source-led map of the cancer settings investigated, the type of evidence available and the questions still unresolved.
scope: Distinct cancer-type/stage chapters; original report and study-family mapping; concurrent anticancer treatment; clinical outcomes, null findings and interactions; unresolved acquisition links
chapters: Identify the cancer type and treatment setting
Keep itraconazole reports and study families distinct
Separate biological hypotheses from patient outcomes
Read clinical comparisons without transferring conclusions
Record missing sources, safety review and unresolved limits
Use a cancer-specific question worksheet
products.readiness: Mandatory owner coverage warrants continued development, but clinical extraction and link reconciliation are incomplete.

products.title: Repurposing and aging claims: human outcomes and open questions
products.description: A guide to reading sirolimus and acarbose research without equating animal lifespan, biomarkers or single-organ outcomes with longer healthy human life.
scope: Sirolimus and acarbose; human versus animal evidence; clinical outcomes versus biomarkers; distinct reproductive, periodontal and exercise questions; interactions and uncertainty
chapters: Distinguish longevity claims from measured human outcomes
Read metformin and sirolimus questions separately
Keep biomarkers distinct from meaningful outcomes
Compare designs and limitations without an overall ranking
Record safety and interaction evidence gaps
Use a worksheet to follow future reviewed updates
products.readiness: The demand sample supports a topic hypothesis, but several questions have sparse or historical-only signals and exact human-use evidence remains incomplete.

products.title: Breast cancer repurposing research: a question-by-question guide
products.description: A planned guide that separates breast-cancer subtype, stage, treatment setting and patient outcomes before assessing any repurposed-drug claim.
scope: Subtype and stage; neoadjuvant/adjuvant/metastatic setting; concurrent standard treatment; primary clinical outcomes and harms; source and family verification; questions for the oncology team
chapters: Define subtype, stage and treatment context before comparing reports
Separate breast-specific studies from other cancer research
Map each candidate to its original human evidence
Read outcomes, comparison groups and uncertainty
Record safety and interaction questions for oncology review
Find unresolved sources and questions for the treating team
products.readiness: Current page has background sources CP019-R01 and CP027-CH14 with no synthesis rows. Acquired F05 materials remain INCOMPLETE and unverified.
